But it was the absent Grealish who dominated the buildup after Everton announced he had been dropped for disciplinary reasons.Grealish is understood to have missed training on Monday without permission. Despite the importance of the fixture and the limited options at his disposal, and the playmaker’s subsequent return to training, Moyes demonstrated that no player is bigger than the club by banishing the 31-year-old from the game. The Everton manager later claimed it was “a club decision” but it was taken by him and the chief executive, Angus Kinnear. Ultimately, and no doubt to Grealish’s great relief, he was not missed.Newcastle dominated the opening 20 minutes to the extent that a two-goal interval lead for Everton would have seemed inconceivable. Pickford saved an early header from Harvey Barnes, who then turned provider to set up Jacob Ramsey for a shot that was blocked superbly by Vitalii Mykolenko. Fabian Schär also tested Pickford from distance, leaving the England international raging at the lack of protection in front of him. He could not fault his defenders’ willingness to put their bodies on the line, however.View image in fullscreenHayden Hackney scores Everton’s second goal against Newcastle.Photograph: Aidan Hunter/Action Plus/ShutterstockEverton gradually turned the contest around. Putting an end to ineffective long balls up to Barry, when he was marked by Dan Burn, helped their cause, although it was a long clearance from Pickford that led to the breakthrough. Amar Dedic looked to retrieve the goalkeeper’s punt but was harried out of possession by Tyrique George. The ball broke to Hackney, who squared inside for Garner to find the far corner of Lukas Hornicek’s goal. “The first goal, it’s no risk, clear it,” said a dismayed Jaissle. “But we concede out of nothing. The first, second and third goals were the same with individual mistakes. We need to be more efficient and learn fast.”Pickford came in for his customary Sunderland stick from the Newcastle support. He responded in the best way possible; with a hand in a second goal that deflated the sizeable away section. The Everton keeper reacted sharply to launch a quick throw towards Dewsbury-Hall in the centre circle. Dewsbury-Hall spun away from Burn before embarking on a determined run that was halted by a trip from behind by Ramsey. The referee, Farai Hallam, played an excellent advantage as the ball broke to Barry. Newcastle appeared to pause, waiting for the free-kick, and were punished when Barry clipped over a cross for Hackney to volley home from close range.A triple half-time substitution from Jaissle was an unmistakable sign of discontent with Newcastle’s ineffective display at both ends of the pitch.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideCarabao Cup quarter-final drawShowFleetwood v EvertonManchester City v Bradford CityCrystal Palace v SunderlandLiverpool v BournemouthTies will take place during the week commencing 14 DecemberWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.There was more menace from the visitors in the second half with the substitute Yoane Wissa having an early chance from Joe Willock’s chip and Dedic’s shot looping over off Hackney’s heel. But with Pickford standing firm and saving smartly from Lewis Hall, Anthony Elanga and Ramsey, and Wissa almost hitting the corner flag with one decent chance, Newcastle’s failure to make their pressure count continued.The visitors were punished when Everton made the game safe in devastating style. Garner, a growing influence, intercepted a pass from Dedic and released Dewsbury-Hall behind a static Newcastle defence. The midfielder took Burn out of the equation with a perfect pass across to Barry, who had time to control and place a fine finish beyond Hornicek.Burn finally broke Everton’s resistance with a late header from an Elanga cross. A melee involving the goalscorer, Pickford, James Tarkowski and Joelinton broke out as they fought over the ball – all four were booked – but there would be no miraculous escape for Newcastle. It is Everton who march on to face the Cod Army.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupEvertonNewcastle Unitedmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy takes shot at ‘horseshit’ Yankees team after World Series win | Milwaukee Brewers | The Guardian
description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy was captured taking a shot at a teh 2023 Yankees after he celebrated his team clinching the World Series
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy was captured taking a shot at a teh 2023 Yankees after he celebrated his team clinching the World Series
Content: Pat Murphy hugs right fielder Sal Frelick after winning the World Series.Photograph: Chris O’Meara/APView image in fullscreenPat Murphy hugs right fielder Sal Frelick after winning the World Series.Photograph: Chris O’Meara/APMilwaukee BrewersBrewers manager Pat Murphy takes shot at ‘horseshit’ Yankees team after World Series winMurphy offers critique of 2023 edition of YankeesHoward Bryant: Brewers expose baseball’s biggest lieGuardian sportThu 29 Oct 2026 11.15 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 15.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMilwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy was captured taking a shot at a “horseshit Yankees team” after he celebrated his teamclinching the World Serieson Wednesday night.A videoof Murphy talking to Jake Bauers emerged in which the manager tells the Brewers’ soon to be a free agent: “You’re going to be a rich fucker. Just remember when you were on that horseshit Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, ‘This is the way we used to do it.’”The low-budget Brewers won the World Series – and exposed baseball’s biggest lie | Howard BryantRead moreBauers played for the Yankees in 2023 before he was traded to the Brewers. The Yankees finished fourth in the AL East in 2023, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2016. Bauers did little to help them, batting .202 with 12 home runs in 84 games that season. However, he has thrived at the Brewers: in the 2026 regular season he hit .266 with 26 home runs and an OPS of .874, all career bests. He was also named the National League Championship Series MVP as the Brewersswept the Los Angeles Dodgersto reach the World Series for the first time since 1982.Murphy also had another excellent season and is favorite to be named the NL Manager of the Year for a third season in a row.Murphy is not the first person to joke about the Yankees in aWorld Series. When the Dodgers overwhelmed the Yankees in the 2024 edition, Los Angeles veteran Joe Kelly said New York were “sloppy” and “can’t make a play”, while his teammate Miguel Rojas called out their “lazy” defense.The Brewers did not limit their attention to the Yankees after their win. Pitcher Trevor Megill was asked if he had a message for his team’s fans after they clinched the World Series.“Have fun talking shit to Chicago next year,”Megill told MLB reporter Ben Verlander. “We have a ring.”Explore more on these topicsMilwaukee BrewersNew York YankeesMLBBaseballUS sportsWorld SeriesnewsShareReuse this content

title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down | Soccer | The Guardian
description: From Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler. Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questions
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: From Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler. Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questions
Content: A viral video of a three-year-old soccer player in Florida has sparked a national debate over youth sports, parental behavior and the perils of internet fame.Photograph: Tim Clayton/Corbis/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA viral video of a three-year-old soccer player in Florida has sparked a national debate over youth sports, parental behavior and the perils of internet fame.Photograph: Tim Clayton/Corbis/Getty ImagesSoccerA three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him downFrom Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler. Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questionsJeff RueterThu 29 Oct 2026 04.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 13.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere is real tragedy in this week’s story of the three-year-old Florida boy whose parents claimed he was so good at soccer that police werecalled to do what opposing defenders couldn’t. But it doesn’t lie where the outrage cycle wants you to think. It’s broader, implicates more people, and to me, is far more depressing.You may have seen thevideoby now. Here was a toddler with fabulous soccer talent, running end-to-end and scoring goal after goal against opponents who have seemingly just found their feet. The cameraman, later identified as the child’s father, loudly and proudly cheers his son on. Way to go, kid.Then, an abrupt cut to the parents speaking with two police officers from the Orlando suburb of Winter Park. “They called the police on a three-year-old, because he’s too good,” one of the parents says. An officer responds: “They’re wanting you guys to head out, OK?” The parents ask: “You’re confused too, right?”In the final shot, his mother says: “This is the biggest part of it. We’re trying to put a show on in front of these people. It’s all on [TikTok] Live. There’s thousands of people watching this. He’s famous. There’s thousands of people watching this.”Police called to Florida soccer game after parents say three-year-old benched for being too goodRead moreThe story quickly became national news. It was easy to see why. It appeared to take in so many flawed aspects of America: the commoditization of youth sports, overbearing parents, police called for seemingly minor infractions, a social media pile-on and race relations (the child and his parents are Black, the majority of the other children and their parents in the clip were white). Celebrities quickly weighed in to give the story even more life, among them US international Alex Freeman and children’s edutainer Ms Rachel. Civil rights attorney Ben Crumpthrew his hat in the ring.But the story is more complicated than the viral video suggested. Police dispatch records, 911 calls and body-camera footage obtained and reviewed by the Guardian offer a fuller picture of what happened on Saturday morning. The organizer, who is also Black, acknowledged that the boy was unusually talented but told officers he had been pushing other children and that his parents had become argumentative. The organizer said he had been rotating players to ensure everyone got a turn, and that the parents had argued with other families. That approach was consistentwith i9 Sports’ stated philosophy, which emphasizes fun, inclusion and equal playing time regardless of ability. In a 911 call obtained by the Guardian, the organizer complained of an allegedly disruptive parent who was following him around, calling him names and livestreaming their confrontation. He also referred to the family’s large Instagram following in remarks captured on body-camera footage. The parents offered a sharply different account, insisting that their son was being unfairly singled out because of his ability. Officers, who had not witnessed the dispute, treated it as a civil matter and discussed arranging a refund. No arrests were made.When the scenes in Winter Park first landed on my feeds on Saturday night, my initial reaction was largely in line with the popular discourse. But even as I learned more, a shot near the end has continued to haunt me. The camera’s edge catches a glimpse of the youngster, visibly confused, already overwhelmed. He couldn’t have known that he’d become a main character of this week’s internet. An audience of mere thousands was about to seem tiny.Neil Postman got famous arguing that modern media amounts to “amusing ourselves to death”. A few generations on, that phrase is showing its age. Not for its core messaging, but for the implication that amusement is the point. Platforms ensnare users with endless scrolling, fueled by algorithms to extract every penny from one’s pocket and every second from one’s existence. Even if this was the worst day of this kid’s life (or, at least, hisworst day so far), that wasn’t the point. The idea that this is an incident with plenty of nuance to consider is immaterial. It was engagement fodder, fresh and meaty ragebait for the ravenous masses to consume and proliferate.View image in fullscreenBody-worn camera footage of police in Winter Park, Florida, responding to a call of a disturbance at a park on Sunday.Photograph: Winter Park PDAt this point, it’s worth acknowledging that even if the initial video had accurately conveyed the reason for the police’s summoning – which, understandably, the parents couldn’t immediately discern – we may have ended up in the same place. There are countless stories ofparents crossing lines at youth sportsevents, including some that weremore worthy of law enforcement. That aspect of this all has largely fallen on deaf ears.The livestream raises another question, too: what about the other children playing that morning, whose images may have been broadcast to thousands of strangers without their parents ever consenting to such exposure? That point would seem salient enough, and is worth a closer look.So quickly has this story gone viral that most of us have overlooked one crucial detail: the player involved at the heart of all this isthree years old. A toddler. By any criteria, the boy is far too young to be platformed like this, whether by his parents or by the various companies that have leapt on to the story: Jay-Z’s sports and entertainment agency Roc Nationhas offered to fly the boy to Spainfor “an impactful athletic experience”.Our culture has ignored any teachable moments from the hype trains that pushed LeBron James, Tiger Woods and Freddy Adu front and center well before they turned 18. Countless parents aspire to turn their children into the next viral sensation, as if that’s a healthy and wise idea. Three-year-olds often can’t keep within the lines of their coloring books, much less understand the ramifications of a grift.As of Wednesday, the young athlete has nearly 900,000 followers on Instagram and 1.2 million on TikTok.One especially ghoulish postfrom Monday shows his likeness thrown into a dozen different AI-generated “ads” to position the toddler as a spokesperson for cereal, sugary drinks and athletic gear.He’s clearly not making these posts himself. It’s hard to imagine he’s asking to become another in an endless and tired trend of athletes turned influencers. Yet his profile has two links: an email address for inquiries –introducing this winter’s hot toy, My Little Inbox– and a GoFundMe to “support [his] soccer journey”, with a claim that this is all about “protecting [his] passion for soccer”. As of Wednesday night, the fundraiser had raised more than $49,000, comfortably surpassing its $30,000 goal.Hopefully he can soon enjoy the anonymity that nearly every other three-year-old enjoys. To grow up as a child rather than as a commodity. To continue playing sports because he loves them, not because there’s a buck to be made.But maybe that window has already slammed shut. There were too many clicks to be generated, too much engagement to be had. In this case, across the board, the grownups and their machines have let him down. The question now is whether they’ll allow him to be a child again.Explore more on these topicsFootballUS sportsSocial mediaFloridaJay-ZfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Everybody hates Pat: is a cabal of college kids really trying to bring down ESPN’s star meathead? | US sports media | The Guardian
description: Pat McAfee’s reaction to a few mild jokes shows how the ubiquitous ESPN host he’s happy to whip up a crowd into a hostile frenzy but is terrified of any criticism
Author: Aaron Timms
Headline: Pat McAfee’s reaction to a few mild jokes shows how the ubiquitous ESPN host he’s happy to whip up a crowd into a hostile frenzy but is terrified of any criticism
Content: Pat McAfee has enjoyed a rapid ascent in the world of sports media.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPat McAfee has enjoyed a rapid ascent in the world of sports media.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesUS sports mediaEverybody hates Pat: is a cabal of college kids really trying to bring down ESPN’s star meathead?Pat McAfee’s reaction to a few mild jokes shows how the ubiquitous ESPN personality is happy to whip up a crowd into a hostile frenzy but is terrified of any criticismAaron TimmsThu 29 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 05.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was all shaping up to be a golden year for Pat McAfee. The man who landed a five-year, $85m deal in 2023 to take The Pat McAfee Show to ESPN had cemented himself as the star attraction of the sports broadcaster’s bold new era of stunts, stupidity andmemebrain swill. His persistently honking presence on the set of ESPN’s College GameDay had helped push ratings to new heights. ESPN executives were so impressed with McAfee they werereportedlyin negotiations to award him a new contract worth between $60m and $65m a year; one even went so far as todescribehim as a “generational” media talent.Then, over the weekend, disaster struck. A handful of college kids attacked him online ahead of his appearance with College GameDay at the University of Utah. Well, “attacked” is maybe overstating things: theymade a few mild jokes at his expense. But it was all too much for ESPN’s brightest blimp. Suddenly, McAfee’s world came crashing down. His initial reaction, to be fair, was mild: “The university’s Instagram account posted something talking a little trash about me last night, which I certainly love,” he said ahead of the Utes’ clash with the Houston Cougars last week.But by Monday the narrative had changed. On his eponymous show, McAfee said he had “never felt more uncomfortable” than he did on the Utah campus, alluding tothe assassination of Charlie Kirkas a reason for his unease: “I thought to myself: Has anything really scary happened at, like, a college gathering in the state of Utah recently? Do you think we should be amplifying reasons for why people hate my guts as a university? I don’t know.”View image in fullscreenPat McAfee flashes Texas Tech’s Guns Up gesture during ESPN’s College GameDay in Lubbock, Texas, last November. His boisterous, crowd-baiting antics have become a fixture of the program, though he has proved less enthusiastic about being on the receiving end of the joke.Photograph: John E Moore III/Getty ImagesWell, Pat, neither do I. To read this comically melodramatic retelling of his time at Utah you might assume last week’s College GameDay was uncommonly vicious and antagonistic. Instead, it was the usual chop-up of hype, half-assed technical analysis and shouting, in which McAfee supplied his standard mix of meandering rants and basic crowd work and the gathered masses, in turn, responded with cheers and (good-natured) boos as expected. Thevideothat McAfee implied had him fearing for his life, posted to the university’s Instagram and TikTok accounts, involved a handful of students poking very light fun at the ESPN host for ripping off his shirt on set (which hedoes often) and spouting “corny” lines in place of real analysis (ditto); one of McAfee’s would-be assassins even emphasized that “we love you bro” as he implored McAfee to “keep the shirt on”.double quotation markFigures like McAfee drag us all back into the frathouse, the kegger, the swamp, and now they won’t even let us joke about itThe wokes and the leftists are always the most precious snowflakes on earth until some kid does a mild impersonation of Pat McAfee ripping his top open; when that happens it’s a federal emergency and the national guard needs to be called in to set things right. Any more of this mild banter from the brutes and ingrates of the American undergraduate population and McAfee will be callinghis buddy Donald Trumpto request Secret Service protection.Even more bizarre than McAfee’s amazingly thin-skinned overreaction to this absolute non-event is howseriouslyhis claims of imminent danger to his life (stemming, once again, from a video in which a few students say they don’t want to see McAfee’s naked torso) have been taken by those around him. The schoolpublished a groveling apologyfor its actions and deleted the offending video from its social media channels, while ESPN issued a statement of support for McAfee and “the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security”.View image in fullscreenPat McAfee alongside Donald Trump at the Patriot Games in Ohio in August. The ESPN star has emerged as one of the most prominent figures in a new generation of rightwing sports personalities aligned with the president.Photograph: Anna Moneymaker/Getty ImagesDuring his ascent at ESPN, McAfee has perfected all the attributes of a WWE-style heel – the gift for offense, the shirtlessness, thepenchant for writhing on the ground like an upturned beetle– with the exception of one: he absolutely cannot stand it when he’s the butt of the joke. The man is a machine at whipping a crowd into a hostile frenzy then runs in fright the moment the first boos hit his ears. McAfee is perhaps the leading light of the rightwing sports bros who’vecome to prominencein the age of Trump: these men love sports,love their country, love their president, and are unsure what to make of women. Trump himself made hisdebut appearanceon The Pat McAfee Show late last year, and over this summer McAfee was on hand to lend some primetime meat to the inauguralPatriot Games, the president’s Hitlerian exercise in uplift for the white youth of America.Clay Travis: inside the Maga permadad’s world of sports bros, trans panic and mortgagesRead moreIt’s perhaps no surprise, then, that McAfee has absorbed completely the personality traits of the president: to the casual misogyny, the constant moaning about “woke”, the boorishness and the egomania can now be added McAfee’s Trumpian inability to take a joke or any kind of criticism, however mild or well-intentioned; in the deranged McAfee worldview it now seems even college kids, a big part of College GameDay’s own audience, are part of the shadowy network of villainy working to bring ESPN’s star beetroot down. Whether it’s punching across at critical media outlets or punching down at fans who don’t like the kind of shirt-ripping frattiness he’s introduced to College GameDay, McAfee never seems more engaged in his work than whensnarlingabout the “rats”, “marks”, “losers” and “puppets” snapping at his feet.It cannot be emphasized too much how stupid and overblown this whole concocted controversy is. What is really going on here? Is this all reflective of a desire for attention on McAfee’s part, another demonstration of his continuous need to make everything – in sport, on TV, in culture at large – About Him? Or is ESPN so heavily degraded and virality-brained now, soin thrall to the Magaverseand its perverse understanding of the world, that the empty suits who run the place genuinely feel the operation will collapse without a happy McAfee – placated and kept safe from the everyday terrorists roving the college campuses of America – at its core?View image in fullscreenESPN personalities Stephen A Smith and Pat McAfee before Monday’s Cowboys-Eagles game in Philadelphia. McAfee’s rise has come to symbolize the network’s embrace of personality-driven spectacle over traditional sports analysis.Photograph: Mitchell Leff/Getty ImagesPerhaps it’s a bit of both. As Soft Pat’s star at ESPN has risen and he’s been handedmore prestigious on-air assignments, the statements emanating from the C-suite hailing his “generational” and otherworldly talent have become more and more ludicrous; amid reports of his monster new contract, McAfee is now involved in Monday Night Football and there’s talk of potentially using his Super Bowl alt-cast for even higher honors on screen.“Pat can do whatever he wants,” ESPN executive vice-president Mike Foss recentlymused, and there’s a real sense that the whole network is under the spell of McAfee’s bare breast, that – if only as a cultural project – the erstwhile “Worldwide Leader in Sports” now belongs to McAfee. The wholesale enrollment of a once-proud network into the cult of McAfee does not reflect the man’s talent: he’s good for ratings, sure, but any old rightwing purplehead could curl up into a topless ball, screeching, and do what he does. Instead, it’s a sign of the profound confusion that has gripped traditional media in the post-cordcutting era of vertical video and endless slop. Nothing else works, seems to be the thinking; maybe this idiot will.In another context, or another era, the TV triumph of the outcast, the oddball, the unlikely star might have heralded a deepening of the culture, a growing sophistication in our collective understanding of what it takes to be appealing as a popular media talent. But so much of what McAfee represents is the kind of meatheaded insensitivity that sports broadcasting – with its polish and professionalism – was historically designed to supersede, especially at a place likeESPN. Figures like McAfee drag us all back into the frathouse, the kegger, the swamp, and now they won’t even let us joke about it.Explore more on these topicsUS sports mediaESPNNFLCollege footballCollege sportsUS television industryUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Bears swing big and trade two first-round picks for star Titans DT Jeffery Simmons | NFL | The Guardian
description: Chicago, who are chasing their first Super Bowl title since 1985, sent two first-round draft picks and a fourth-round pick in exchange for the eighth-year veteran
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chicago, who are chasing their first Super Bowl title since 1985, sent two first-round draft picks and a fourth-round pick in exchange for the eighth-year veteran
Content: Jeffery Simmons was a first-team All-Pro selection last season with the Titans.Photograph: Jeff Roberson/APView image in fullscreenJeffery Simmons was a first-team All-Pro selection last season with the Titans.Photograph: Jeff Roberson/APNFLBears swing big and trade two first-round picks for star Titans DT Jeffery SimmonsStruggling Tennessee get haul of picks for tackleChicago are chasing first Super Bowl title since 1985Associated PressThu 29 Oct 2026 12.22 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 12.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Chicago Bears have acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in a blockbuster trade with theTennessee Titans, a person familiar with the deal told the Associated Press on Thursday.The Bears sent their first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, along with a fourth-rounder in next year’s draft, to the Titans for Simmons and a fifth-round selection in 2028.The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal had not been announced.The NFL has a host of Hall of Fame caliber receivers. But which one is the best?Read moreLed by Caleb Williams, Chicago have won two in a row to improve to 5-2 going into Monday night’s game at Seattle. They are chasing the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North, and the addition of Simmons bolsters what had a been a questionable defensive line.The Bears won the division last year for the first time since 2018, finishing with an 11-6 record in coach Ben Johnson’s first season in charge. They advanced in the playoffs by edging the Green Bay Packers in a wild-card game before losing to the Los Angeles Rams in overtime in the divisional round.The pricey trade for Simmons is another signal that Johnson and general manager Ryan Poles think the team have what it takes to win the franchise’s first Super Bowl title since 1985.Asked Wednesday about his role with theNFLtrade deadline coming up on 10 November, Johnson said there was “a lot going on.”“That’s certainly Ryan’s domain, and yet we have constant dialogue of what this team needs and where we can impact ourselves not just this year but years in the future as well,” Johnson said. “He’s turning over every stone that he possibly can to improve this football team just like he has ever since I’ve gotten in this building and I feel really good about our process. We’ll see what happens.”The 29-year-old Simmons has four sacks in seven games this season. He was a first-team All-Pro selection last year, when he had a career-high 11 sacks in 15 games.“Each and every day I wake up, my goal is to just be where my feet are at,” Simmons said Wednesday when asked about the possibility of being traded, “never looking ahead right now, it’s just be in the moment, and that’s from each and every day, from game day, my goal just never changes. I don’t worry about the things I can’t control. Them types of things are a distraction.”Explore more on these topicsNFLChicago BearsTennessee TitansUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them? | Soccer | The Guardian
description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma
Author: Leander Schaerlaeckens
Headline: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma
Content: Dortmund fans were incentivized to keep their phones away for a recent home match against Eintracht.Photograph: Leon Kuegeler/ReutersView image in fullscreenDortmund fans were incentivized to keep their phones away for a recent home match against Eintracht.Photograph: Leon Kuegeler/ReutersSoccerA phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?Leander SchaerlaeckensIt makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemmaThu 29 Oct 2026 13.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 13.02 EDTShareBy all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them.And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop theBundesligastandings.Yet, apparently, a crisis of a sort has been churning just below the surface of what is, by broad consensus, Europe’s best home support.On Friday, Dortmund hadannounceda kind of bribery scheme. A rewards program is probably a kinder way of putting it. Fans who stayed off their phones during the bout with Eintracht had the chance to win signed jerseys and earn gift cards to the club’s merchandise store. If they activated a so-called “fan mode” on the club’s app – a name so phenomenally passive-aggressive you can only applaud whoever came up with it – the club could count who unlocked their phones the fewest times during the game. For every minute the fans left their phones alone, they got points.Dortmund are not the only German team to pick a fight with phones.Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander SchaerlaeckensRead moreSecond-division clubs Hertha Berlin and Dynamo Dresden have banned commercial influencer-style videos in their stadiums altogether, fearing for both the integrity of the TV rights they sell and the experience of their fans. Dortmund, likewise, appear motivated by the incursion of influencers, who are siphoning off and monetizing footage of the famous match-day experience and growing into a nuisance for regulars.This problem has also afflicted the tennis majors. The US Open now resemblesan influencer conventionmore than it does a tennis tournament. When the US Tennis Association credentialed more than 100 content creators this year, the influencers grew so disruptive that a match was stopped when a chair umpire had to ask them to turn off a ring light. Wimbledon hasrefusedto credential influencers for just this reason, which doesn’t stop them from getting in with regular tickets or through sponsors.Dortmund’s attempt at shaping fan behavior, however, goes further than warding off the cultural content parasites. Thisplease-stop-holding-up-your-phones-and-just-live-in-the-presentplea raises quasi-existential questions about sport and its consumption.“Over 81,000 people in the stadium, singing, cheering, and holding their breath together: this here and now is irreplaceable,” Dortmund chief executive Carsten Cramersaid. “And that’s exactly what we’re putting front and center together.”“Anyone at a soccer game should experience the moment and the emotions – not just a cell phone screen,” added Marcel de Groot, the chief executive of Vodafone Germany, both a cellphone service provider and a Dortmund sponsor. “Let’s leave our smartphones in our pockets more often at the stadium and instead focus on what’s happening on the field and in the stands.”These were statements delivered with unshakeable confidence in their righteousness, yet there is evidence to suggest this simply isn’t how some fans want to behave at stadiums.Which begs the question: can, and should, professional sports teams get to dictatehowtheir ticket-buying fans experience their games? It’s surely a question that’s crossed the mind of all the musicians who now perform to a sea of cell phones, their flashlights on, obscuring the faces in the crowd. Did their fans buy the right to experience the concert as they please? Or does this objectify the musicians and diminish the performance, somehow?View image in fullscreenThe incentives didn’t keep all Dortmund fans from using their phones at the match.Photograph: Christopher Neundorf/EPAIt goes back to the question of whether sport is entertainment, and whether its consumers get to sit back and let the proceedings and the attendant stimuli wash over them. Or whether they are something else entirely: active participants in the games they attend. If that is so, then fandom amounts to a parasocial relationship conferring membership to a community with attendant behavioral expectations.What are the responsibilities of the ticketholder? Do teams get to purity-test their supporters? What do fans owe their teams? Is live soccer just content? A day out, not unlike going to the movies or a museum, where nobody expects total focus and for you to cheer on the thing you’re looking at? Is it heresy to even suggest this?The latter tends to be the view, or at least the vibe, in most American sports leagues where fans are often less engaged, told by an announcer and a jumbo screen when and what to clap or stomp or chant. This has always contrasted with the feel of global football, where the folklore is usually organic, sparked and dictated by the fans themselves. It’s why all of those pre-game andhalf-time concertsat the World Cup final rankled, drowning out the thrum of the throaty Argentina fans.It feels both instructive and fitting that this debate broke out at Dortmund. The Bundesliga’s rules on safeguarding fan majority ownership of very nearly every club have preserved the league as a kind of supporters’ paradise, with relatively cheap tickets and policies that put fans first. Dortmund, for their part, have been held up for years as a paradigm for their following – thus attracting the influencers, of course.The latter will be dealt with, it seems. In an age when soccer clubs are essentially production houses who also field company teams, it always seemed inevitable that these interlopers would be expelled from the premises. The fans, however, are not so easily corrected on behavior their teams have deemed undesirable. And they will vote with their credit cards.Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: U.S. Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts,which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.Explore more on these topicsFootballBundesligaEuropean club footballUS sportscommentShareReuse this content

title: The NFL has a host of Hall of Fame caliber receivers. But which one is the best? | NFL | The Guardian
description: Quarterbacks in 2026 have a series of dazzling weapons at their disposal. We rank the best of the receivers in the NFL at the moment
Author: Graham Searles
Headline: Quarterbacks in 2026 have a series of dazzling weapons at their disposal. We rank the best of the receivers in the NFL at the moment
Content: Puka Nacua and Justin Jefferson greet each other after a game in 2024.Photograph: Michael Owens/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPuka Nacua and Justin Jefferson greet each other after a game in 2024.Photograph: Michael Owens/Getty ImagesNFLThe NFL has a host of Hall of Fame caliber receivers. But which one is the best?Quarterbacks in 2026 have a series of dazzling weapons at their disposal. We rank the best of the receivers in the NFL at the momentGraham SearlesThu 29 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 12.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNB: We have restricted the list below to players in their prime years, so excellent, older receivers such as Mike Evans and Davante Adams have been left out.1) Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seattle SeahawksThe quality of receivers across theNFLat present is sky high. And Smith-Njigba is a cut above the rest. There are faster and more physical wideouts, but none have the precise, impossible to cover route running of JSN. Most receivers have a tell that hints at their next move. Not Smith-Njigba though: defensive backs have to guess and second guess his movements, which leads to consistent, easy separation and massive yardage totals.Jaxon Smith-Njigba statsThe 24-year-old’s talent is so great that he quickly ended DK Metcalf’s time in Seattle and took over the offense, leading them to the Super Bowl last season. Smith-Njigba is the key to Seattle’s offense, not Sam Darnold at quarterback. Any league average passer could be elevated to playoff success throwing to Smith-Njigba.After seven games this season he is closing in on 1,000 receiving yards. He almost broke 1,800 yards in 2025 but, at this pace, he could be the first NFL receiverto crack 2,000 yards in a season.2) Puka Nacua, Los Angeles RamsNot a lot was thought of Nacua heading into the 2023 draft. He was seen as a decent option as a slot receiver or a gadget guy. NFL analyst Lance Zierlein’s assessmentwasn’t exactly glowing: “Nacua is an athletic wideout lacking the twitch or speed to attack man coverage at a successful rate. However, the ball skills and competitive nature he brings to the field give him a fighting chance to make a roster.”Chiefs sign Justin Tucker in wake of sexual misconduct allegations as Butker strugglesRead moreTeams were put off by his lack of speed – his 40-yard dash was the 37th-best among wide receivers drafted in 2023 – and he fell to the Rams in the fifth round. But the NFL isn’t all about straight-line speed. He did well in the combine’s gauntlet drill – which involves running across the field while catching balls fired from either side – and Nacua reached the highest top speed of any receiver who did not miss a catch.What’s even more special is how quickly he adapted to the NFL. His first game: 10 receptions for 119 yards. Lucky start? Nope. Game two: 147 yards. He had an off day on his third outing with “only” 72 yards. Game four he roared back with 163 yards and a touchdown. The only knock on the 25-year-old is his availability – he has only played all 17 games once in his career – and hehas been mired in off-field issues. But when he’s on the field he has been ultra consistent, and could go for 1,500 yards this year, despite missing a couple of games.3) Ja’Marr Chase, Cincinnati BengalsThe Bengals top receiver in yards this season is Tee Higgins by a wide margin, but Chase is still the leader – alongside Joe Burrow – of Cincinnati’s offense. That includes in the locker room too. On Sunday, Chase gave a stirring half-time speech after the Bengals went into the break 13-0 down.“I came in here screaming, saying, ‘Somebody’s got to make a play for us, somebody got to make a play,’” Chase said after the game. “And I told our offense we can’t look at our defense the whole time. We’ve got to step this shit up and make something work.”And they did. The Bengals scored five unanswered touchdowns to obliterate the Ravens for a vital victory in the ultra competitive AFC North. Chase’s elite speed, agility and phenomenal hands are a nightmare for defenders. He often starts seasons slowly, so expect great things to come from a player capable of unparalleled production. Chase’s has three career games of 200 or more receiving yards, the best in the NFL among active players.4) Justin Jefferson, Minnesota VikingsThe Vikings star is in a tricky spot. His talent is undeniable, as is his track record. At the start of the season his 8,480 yards receiving since 2020 were the most for any player in the first six years of their career. That total includes last year though, when Jefferson recorded his lowest total for receiving yards, touchdowns and first downs. Then again, he did have JJ McCarthy, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer throwing him the ball.Justin Jefferson statsAnd in another season in which Minnesota’s defense is doing the heavy lifting, Jefferson is still on good form despite an uninspiring cast of quarterbacks. He already has more touchdowns (3) than he did in the whole of last season, and there are signs that Kyler Murray could be able to give him the service he deserves.Against the Saints, Murray went all-in witha fastball to Jeffersonin the back of the endzone amid blanket coverage. It all looked so simple as Jefferson popped and came down with the ball, while falling backwards, for the touchdown. Hopefully Murray can give Jefferson a few more moments like that as the 6-0 Vikings builds towards the playoffs.The best of the restZay Flowers, Amon-Ra St Brown, Chris Olave, CeeDee Lamb, Christian Watson, (honorary tight end inclusion) Trey McBride and Higgins all have a case here but Drake London gets the nod owing to untapped potential and immense physicality. He always appears to be open, thanks to a 6ft 4in frame, brilliant hands and great route running. He lacks speed but the 25-year-old is as close as it gets to a Mike Evans clone. He would be accruing similarly impressive stats if the Atlanta Falcons had more competent quarterback play. A rogues gallery of Desmond Ridder, Kirk Cousins, Marcus Mariota, Taylor Heinicke and Cooper Rush have stymied London’s numbers since he joined the NFL in 2022, but in 19 games with Michael Penix at quarterback he has 1,822 yards and 10 touchdowns. Penix is good but by no means great, and London still has much more to offer.Explore more on these topicsNFLSeattle SeahawksCincinnati BengalsMinnesota VikingsLos Angeles RamsUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Tara Elimbi Gilbert’s late equaliser came moments after Khadija Shaw scored a penalty as Manchester City drew their third league phase game in a row
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Tara Elimbi Gilbert’s late equaliser came moments after Khadija Shaw scored a penalty as Manchester City drew their third league phase game in a row
Content: Tara Elimbi Gilbert is embraced by her PSG teammates after scoring a late equaliser.Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Uefa/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTara Elimbi Gilbert is embraced by her PSG teammates after scoring a late equaliser.Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Uefa/Getty ImagesWomen's Champions LeaguePSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopesTom Garryat the Joie StadiumThu 29 Oct 2026 18.14 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 19.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleYou cannot miss half a dozen big chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’ wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to secure a point at a disappointed Joie Stadium.City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim.Manchester City 1-1 Paris Saint-Germain: Women’s Champions League – as it happenedRead moreThey thought they had won the game through Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s 85th-minute penalty, but conceding sparked PSG into life and they snatched a point with a scrappy equaliser three minutes later as their substitute Tara Elimbi Gilbert found the net from close range.How, therefore, should we look upon City’s season? Are they the team that is unbeaten in all competitions? Or the team without a win in Europe? Both ring true, and although they are still likely to progress to the knockout stages, they will have been hugely frustrated with their profligacy.“There are a lot of things in this game we are pleased with. The result is not what we wanted, of course. Maybe we should kill the game earlier,” the City manager, Andrée Jeglertz, reflected. “Annoying is not the right word but it’s a little bit a feeling of ‘argh’. We deserved more, I think, but that’s how it is in the Champions League. When you dominate games and you don’t score, the opponent will take their chances and that’s what they did.”View image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw converts her penalty to give Manchester City the lead.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PADrawsaway to Bayern Munichand athome against Real Madridin their first two games were certainly not poor results, against strong opposition and with theoretically kinder fixtures to come, so there was no need to panic, but City’s 11th-placed position in the table, only one above the final qualification spot, before kick-off will nonetheless have looked a little concerning to some of their supporters. They ended the night 10th.Jeglertz was positive about their chances: “We got drawn against six teams and we have played the three toughest of them, I think, so now we have three games that we have the opportunity, again, to get the points we need to qualify for the next round. So that’s our goal and nothing has changed.”Nonetheless, this latest draw was a blow. PSG sought to frustrate City in the first half, and succeeded after riding out an early storm. Shaw’s header dropped wide at the far post from Aoba Fujino’s third-minute cross, as the home side made a bright start but were unable to score while on top. Shaw fizzed a low strike narrowly wide 11 minutes later after terrific play from Lauren Hemp. City controlled possession but did not test the PSG goalkeeper, Oliwia Peda, until the second half.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideRoundup: Barcelona stay perfect, Juventus win again, Paris FC and Häcken drawShowBarcelonalaid down another marker in their defence of the Women’s Champions League with an 8-0 win thrashing of the Danish champions,HB Køge.A Caroline Graham Hansen penalty and a goal from Ewa Pajor, who finished second in the Ballon d'Or behind her recently departed teammate Alexia Putellas, had the holders in command by half-time in Denmark. Esmee Brugts, Patri Guijarro, Clara Serrajordi, Kika Nazareth and Clàudia Pina, who grabbed a brace, all scored in the second half to complete the rout.Barcelona, who won the women's club award at the Ballon d'Or to go with Pere Romeu's coach of the year prize,  remain top of the league phase with three wins from three by an aggregate score of 19-2, while despite the heavy defeat Køge remain in the playoff places.Juventusstruck twice late on to get the better ofAustria Vienna4-1. Goals by Matilde Pavan and Alba Redondo put Juve seemingly in control before Lotta Cordes reduced the deficit with 12 minutes left, but Kysha Sylla and Júlia Bartel struck in the final nine minutes. This second straight away win puts Juventus fifth, a point off the last automatic quarter-final qualification spot, while Austria Vienna sit 15th and two points off the playoffs.Paris FCandHäckenshared the spoils in the French capital after Anna Anvegard scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time to cancel out Evelyne Viens’ early opener and grab the Swedish champions their first point in Europe this season. They and Paris FC both remain outside the playoff spots.Photograph: Sebastian Elias Uth/Ritzau Scanpix DenmarkWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.This tricky game came in a testing week for City, sandwiched between last Sunday’s Manchester derby – wherethey dropped points for the first timethis season after conceding a late equaliser – and this Sunday’s mouthwatering game away to in-form London City Lionesses and theirBallon d’Or winner, Alexia Putellas, who sit just one place and three points behind them in the WSL. Nobody in sky blue could afford to think about that game yet, though – PSG were no pushovers.Straight after the restart, Fujino went close as she latched onto Kerstin Casparij’s clever ball and shot over from a tight angle. Fujino, a livewire throughout the night, also saw a shot blocked by Thiniba Samoura, as the hosts began to ask tougher questions. Soon they were creating chance after chance.Shaw’s powerful low shot was turned behind by Peda. From the resulting corner, curled in expertly by Alex Greenwood, Shaw had a free header but was unable to connect. Mary Fowler then scuffed wide as frustrations began to mount. Shaw headed wide again moments later.Surely the WSL’s top goalscorer was not going to fire a blank? Indeed not. She finally broke the deadlock after winning a spot-kick, brought down by Griedge Mbock Bathy, and then fired her penalty low to the keeper’s right. But that triggered PSG to attack with vigour for the first time in the match and they were soon level, bursting the City bubble.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueManchester City WomenParis Saint-Germain WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro | Milan | The Guardian
description: Internazionale and Milan have revealed more details about their 71,500-seat stadium which will replace San Siro as their shared home
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Internazionale and Milan have revealed more details about their 71,500-seat stadium which will replace San Siro as their shared home
Content: An image of the planned new stadium, designed by Norman Foster and David Manica, which will be built on the San Siro site.Photograph: Foster + PartnersView image in fullscreenAn image of the planned new stadium, designed by Norman Foster and David Manica, which will be built on the San Siro site.Photograph: Foster + PartnersMilanInter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San SiroGenerali Stadium will have 71,500-seat capacityInter fans protest the plans outside gala eventAgence France-PresseThu 29 Oct 2026 17.46 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 18.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInternazionale and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season.The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2 billion (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.Alessandro Costacurta: ‘San Siro is an icon – it’s incredibly beautiful but it’s not functional’Read moreShortly before the briefing began, a group of Inter fans walked into the courtyard of the castle and unfurled a banner reading “you will never extinguish the lights at San Siro,” and chanting “hands off San Siro.” Work on the new stadium is set to begin in 2028, on the site of the existing 75,000-capacity venue.The Generali Stadium will be shaped “low in the body, and rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said. David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project, added that the steep-sided design aims to bring fans as close to the pitch as possible.“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that San Siro is a feeling,” Manica said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling … we brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass.”View image in fullscreenAn artist’s impression of a concourse inside the planned 71,500-capacity arena.Photograph: Foster + PartnersThe stadium will also be capable of hosting NFL international games, rugby matches and concerts. Milan and Inter paid €197 million (£165m) to acquire the current San Siro stadium and its adjacent parking arenas. The current ground will be largely demolished once construction work nears completion.Also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, San Siro opened in 1926 and is the largest sports stadium in Italy. It is considered to be one of European football’s most iconic venues, but requires extensive modernisation despite undergoing a number of renovations during its lifespan.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Generali Stadium could be used as a venue for Euro 2032, which is being jointly hosted by Italy and Turkey. Foster and Manica previously worked together on the new Wembley Stadium, while the architect’s Foster + Partners firm also designed the plans for Manchester United’s proposed new 100,000-capacity home.Additional reporting from Associated PressExplore more on these topicsMilanInternazionaleSerie AEuropean club footballArchitecturenewsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa close to selecting candidate to run against Infantino in Fifa election | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: Uefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino in the Fifa election and could approve the challenger next week
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Uefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino in the Fifa election and could approve the challenger next week
Content: Gianni Infantino has embarked on an international effort to recover his position after the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino has embarked on an international effort to recover his position after the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/ReutersGianni InfantinoUefa close to selecting candidate to run against Infantino in Fifa electionChallenger’s identity could be approved by next weekArsène Wenger not thought to have entered reckoningExclusive byNick AmesandMatt HughesThu 29 Oct 2026 14.41 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 16.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidate to run againstGianni Infantinoin the Fifa election and could select the challenger as early as next week.The clock is ticking on efforts to oppose Infantino in March, with candidates required to confirm they are standing by 18 November, but there is growing confidence those attempts are nearing a successful resolution. Discussions with potential nominees have gained momentum despite recent setbacks that included a U-turn by the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa,who surprisingly endorsed Infantino’spush for a fourth term.Should an opponent’s identity be confirmed, it will be presented to Uefa’s executive committee and in an online meeting of the confederation’s FA heads. There remains an appetite to leave any announcement until as close to the deadline as possible, largely to head off the possibility of a “dirty tricks” campaign byFifaagainst the proposed candidate, but some sources believe the relevant meetings may be called in the next seven days.Although Arsène Wenger has been among the high-profile names mooted, and is highly favoured as a potential unity candidate in some European football circles, the former Arsenal manager is not believed to have seriously entered the reckoning. Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, could be found at the Fifa Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan this week extolling the virtues of his employer’s new tournament.Anyone confirming their desire to stand will have to tackle severe doubts about the prospects of defeating Infantino, who has embarkedon an international effortto recover his position in recent weeks after being heavily damaged by the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scandal. They would need to add a substantial number of votes from Asia, Concacaf and Africa to the European bloc, which itself may not be taken for granted in a secret ballot, to reach the 106 required.There has been growing cynicism in some corners about the prospects of unseating Infantino in an election, one argument being that a more effective strategy would be a mass boycott or abstention from the vote in Rabat. A view exists that this would isolate Infantino, who has never hidden the fact that his organisation is dependent on Europe for vast amounts of its revenue. Now he finds it in a form of administrative paralysis. The 2029 men’s Club World Cup, currently without a host, is among the events stuck in a deep freeze with little progress being made on its shape or location.View image in fullscreenAleksander Ceferin is a strong critic of Gianni Infantino’s actions.Photograph: Mark Pain/AlamyBut there remains a determination to face down Infantino in March, with some close to the process pointing out that events may have turned further against the Fifa president by then. Infantino faces the spectre of Uefa’s application to four courts in the US for the release of documents pertainingto the failed FFE scheme, with a view to lodging a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement. Fifa has accused Uefa of “harassment” and “misinformation” and denied wrongdoing by Infantino.A preliminary ruling is expected in the coming weeks, although the prospect of Fifa appealing against any decision that goes against it means the process may be extended. ShouldUefamake significant progress with the case, any election or candidature process may come to feel inconsequential.Fifa has until Monday, a deadline set by Uefa, to respond to 42 questions regarding its governance and decision making. Those include issues surrounding FFE, the Fifa peace prize and the suspension ofFolarin Balogun’s banat the World Cup. The Guardian understands Uefa is yet to receive any response. Infantino said last week that Fifa would “answer all the questions posed, to the extent that the process allows and to the best of our ability”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe US midterms, which will be held on Tuesday, may provide further hope for Infantino’s opponents. In July Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee, launched an investigation into links between Infantino, Fifa and the Trump administration. He asked Infantino to provide relevant documents and sit for a transcribed interview, although that is yet to take place. Should the Democrats flip the House, currently controlled by the Republicans, his quest may receive fresh impetus.Regardless, the period before 18 November feels critical for Uefa and its president, Aleksander Ceferin. The Slovene has driven a hardline approach against Fifa’s leadership, which he restated in his “Emperor’s New Clothes” polemic against Infantino at the general assembly of European Football Clubs in Copenhagen last month. Fielding a viable candidate would go a long way towards underlining its credibility.A repeat of Uefa’s climbdown on the eve of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, when it withdrew its threat to boycott the competition, would prove damaging. The extensive autumn charm offensive launched by Infantino has included visits to Latvia, Czechia and Azerbaijan.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoUefaFifaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout | Soccer | The Guardian
description: The Scottish Premiership has made the first move in a likely attempt by the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Scottish Premiership has made the first move in a likely attempt by the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout
Content: The Scottish Premiership is aiming to broadcast all matches from its next rights cycle from 2029.Photograph: Vagelis Georgariou/Action Plus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe Scottish Premiership is aiming to broadcast all matches from its next rights cycle from 2029.Photograph: Vagelis Georgariou/Action Plus/ShutterstockSoccerScottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackoutLeague to invite bids to televise all games from 2029UK leagues expected to coordinate move to end blackoutMatt HughesThu 29 Oct 2026 13.29 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 16.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheScottish Premiershiphas made the first move in what is expected to be a coordinated attempt from the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all of its matches in the next rights cycle from 2029.A tender document issued by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) last week is understood to have given broadcasters an option to bid for live rights to all matches, including games kicking off at 3pm on Saturdays, the domestic broadcast of which is currently prohibited under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.The Guardian revealed last year that the Premier League and English Football League wereeager for the blackout to be liftedbecause they have concluded that selling more matches to broadcasters is the best way to raise revenues, a view that also appears to have taken hold in Scotland.The SPFL’s invitation to tender, first reported bySports Business, is understood to give bidders the flexibility to bid on the basis of the blocked hours governed by Article 48 not being in place.A source with knowledge of the tender said it appeared increasingly unlikely that the four British Football Associations would apply blocked hours in their territories after 2029.UK broadcasters are prevented from showing live football between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays when 50% of games in the top two divisions take place during that period, a provision that means 3pm kick-offs can be broadcast on FA Cup weekends and on weekend bank holidays over Christmas.The UK is the last country in Europe to invoke Article 48, which allows associations to stipulate a period during which matches cannot be televised live in their territory.While the English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish FAs are responsible for applying Article 48, they will be guided by the wishes of the clubs.UK broadcasters can currently show up to 270 Premier League matches, 1,059 EFL games and 82 from the Scottish Premiership, amounting to 35% of fixtures across the season.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Premier League chief executive, Richard Masters, said in August the subject of lifting Article 48 was a live discussion. “We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change,” he told TalkSport. “It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do. I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”Explore more on these topicsFootballScottish PremiershipSports rightsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as captain and says he needs no assurances on United future | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy and is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Michael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy and is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach
Content: Michael Carrick said: ‘I care about what the supporters think. I care about what it feels like in the stadium.’Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick said: ‘I care about what the supporters think. I care about what it feels like in the stadium.’Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedCarrick keeps Fernandes as captain and says he needs no assurances on United futureCarrick says he is not surprised to still be head coachHe describes Fernandes as ‘important’ for the squadWill UnwinThu 29 Oct 2026 10.50 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 12.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy after dropping him for thedefeat by Bournemouthand that he is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach.Carrick and Fernandesheld talksthis week after the Portuguesecriticised the tacticsin the loss to Como, resulting in the midfielder being an unused substitute on Sunday. Harry Maguire took the armband but will not retain it for Saturday’s game at Chelsea, with Carrick saying “there is no decision to be made” and praising Fernandes.Howe, Nagelsmann, Pochettino: can anyone end Manchester United’s doom loop?Read more“He’s an important player for this group,” he said. “He has been and he will be. Between us, we’ve got to make a difference and we’ve got to push things in a good direction. He’s fully committed to this football club, he’s fully committed to making things better. It doesn’t change for me. He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that.”Carrick’s future remains unclear but he has beengiven a chanceto turn around United’s form. The hierarchy held talks over whether to stick with Carrick at the start of the week after eight games without a win, including a wait of more than two months for a Premier League victory. There is keen interest inEddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmannas potential replacements.“I don’t need any assurances from anyone,” Carrick said. “I totally get the position, I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that.”Asked whether he was surprised still to be in charge, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do my job. I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”The United supporters cheered Carrick off after the Bournemouth game, turning their anger on the players, who were booed at Old Trafford. “I care about what the supporters think,” Carrick said. “I care about what it feels like in the stadium, and them travelling for games, to come and see us and support us.“I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see. I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionUnited will be without the striker Benjamin Sesko until the new year because of a shin injury but Carrick was boosted by Kobbie Mainoo’s return to training this week.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Max Dowman to miss three games after Arsenal’s red card appeal rejected | Arsenal | The Guardian

Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The teenager was sent off for lashing out in the defeat at Fleetwood, and the club’s claims over the card and the length of the ban were both dismissed
Content: Max Dowman’s reaction to a tackle in Arsenal’s stunning loss to Fleetwood has earned him a three-match ban.Photograph: James Harrison/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenMax Dowman’s reaction to a tackle in Arsenal’s stunning loss to Fleetwood has earned him a three-match ban.Photograph: James Harrison/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockArsenalMax Dowman to miss three games after Arsenal’s red card appeal rejectedTeenager was sent off for lashing out in Fleetwood defeatClub’s claims over card and ban were both dismissedPress AssociationThu 29 Oct 2026 13.57 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 19.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal’s appeal against Max Dowman’s red card intheir Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwoodand the three-match suspension imposed has been rejected by an independent commission.The 16-year-old Dowman was sent off for a kick out at Harrison Neal following a bruising tackle in the 85th minute of the game, which Fleetwood won on penalties after a 1-1 draw.Max Dowman’s Fleetwood fracas leaves him, Arsenal and Arteta red-facedRead moreArsenal subsequently lodged an appeal, but the Football Association confirmed on Thursday an independent commission had dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Dowman.As a result, Dowman will be suspended for Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as well as their home game with Hull and trip to Newcastle either side of the international break.The FA said the written reasons for the commission’s decision to dismiss the claims would be published in due course.The Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta, said after Tuesday’s match he had not spoken to Dowman about his dismissal, but added: “When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate, it was very clear.”After Fleetwood’s keeper, Jay Lynch, saved Bruno Guimarães’ penalty, 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey stepped up to fire the hosts into the quarter-finals with one of the biggest upsets in the competition’s history. Fleetwood will host another Premier League side, Everton, in the last eight.Arsenal fell behind to Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s 21st-minute strike in a disjointed first-half performance after Arteta made nine changes.The captain, Martin Ødegaard, came on at half-time and Viktor Gyökeres quickly levelled, but Dowman was dismissed before Lynch starred in the shootout to secure a memorable victory.Explore more on these topicsArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea’s fine finishing has them flying high – but how long can it last? | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Despite being at opposite ends of the table, according to expected points data, Chelsea have performed worse than Saturday’s opponents Manchester United.
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Despite being at opposite ends of the table, according to expected points data, Chelsea have performed worse than Saturday’s opponents Manchester United.
Content: Morgan Rogers has scored four Premier League goals for Chelsea, but he is not outscoring his xG figure by as much as last season.Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenMorgan Rogers has scored four Premier League goals for Chelsea, but he is not outscoring his xG figure by as much as last season.Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/ShutterstockChelseaChelsea’s fine finishing has them flying high – but how long can it last?Despite being at opposite ends of the table, according to Opta’s expected points model, Chelsea have performed worse than Saturday’s opponents Manchester UnitedAndrew BeasleyThu 29 Oct 2026 13.21 EDTLast modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 14.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick will arrive at Stamford Bridge on Saturday with the air of a dead man walking. Yet despiteManchester Unitedbeing fifth-bottom of the Premier League and Chelsea fifth-top, the Blues have performed worse this season according to Opta’s expected points model.Is there a glitch in the matrix? Has the fabled supercomputer clicked on a suspicious link? Even though the margin between their data is small, it feels unthinkable thatChelseacould be below United’s level.That is until you review a few statistics. Xabi Alonso’s side held healthy expected goal margins in their wins over Fulham, Brighton and Everton, but were heavily outgunned against Arsenal and Brentford. The xG count went slightly against them versus Hull, Bournemouth and Tottenham, which is concerning when all three were at home in matches they would reasonably expect to win.Chart showing expected goal difference in Chelsea’s Premier League games this seasonOpta’s data suggests Chelsea are the 12th-best team in thePremier League. They have risen to fifth by virtue of a hot finishing streak. Chelsea have scored 6.7 goals more than the quality of their chances imply they deserve, second only to Brighton (6.8), or above them if penalties are excluded. Chelsea scored five times from 10 shots against Bournemouth; while not without precedent, managing so many goals from so few efforts happens less than once a season in the Premier League.Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progressRead moreJordan Henderson has scored twice from five shots outside the box, after finding the net once for every 20 long-range efforts he attempted between 2014 and last season. Pedro Neto’s total of three league goals is two shy of his career best for a Premier League campaign. Morgan Rogers outscoring his expected goals figure is not unusual but he is ahead by 1.87 when he was up 3.15 across the whole of last season. This trio are unlikely to maintain such hot form across another 30 league games.Adding in João Pedro gives Chelsea four of the 12 players who are above their non-penalty xG by at least 1.5 in the Premier League this season. The two league games the Brazilian missed are the two in which Chelsea failed to score, mustering a combined 1.3 expected goals across those matches (against Brentford and Tottenham). João Pedro’s return from injury cannot come soon enough for the club.This is not least because he provides a good focal point for the frontline, even when he is not scoring. Data fromGradient Sportsshows João Pedro has had possession in the opposition penalty area 5.7 times per 90 minutes this season, the most among centre-forwards with at least 400 minutes in the Premier League. Despite playing in wide areas, Estêvão Willian’s average for this metric is 5.8 since joining Chelsea. No single stat can justify a player’s inclusion but the teenager is being omitted when he offers something the team lack in João Pedro’s absence.Chart showing possessions in the box per 90 minutes by centre-forwards in the 2026‑27 Premier LeagueKeeping possession in the penalty area has become increasingly difficult for Chelsea, who have dwindled after a positive start. Third in the division for opposition box touches after four matches, they now sit eighth. While Premier League home teams are averaging 27 touches per match in the box, Chelsea had 17 in their previous two games at Stamford Bridge. Given their possession average is markedly lower than in any recent campaign, it could prove difficult to increase their penalty area activity.Chart showing Chelsea’s possession average by season in the Premier League since 2014-15Alonso has overseen three league matches in which Chelsea had a maximum 38% possession; he had four such games in almost three years at Leverkusen. This is not as game-state driven as you might assume. Chelsea had 40.8% possession at the point they went 3-1 up at Fulham, 34.6% thereafter. They raced into a 3-0 lead against Brighton despite attempting 28.4% of the total passes to that point.This cannot be by design when Alonso’s Bundesliga-winning Leverkusen team topped the German possession standings with 61.8%. He acknowledged as much when quizzed on the issue before Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield. “You want to have possession,”Alonso said. “Knowing the context, knowing what we are building, I think that we have room for improvement in that part. We need to play more confidently with the ball.”History shows Champions League qualification is unlikely with Chelsea’s 46.5% possession. The miracle of Leicester’s title win provides the only instance from the past 12 seasons of a team finishing in the top four with a lower possession average. Beyond that, West Ham finishing sixth in 2020-21 is the best showing.Things may improve once the tactical plan becomes embedded and the lineup settles. Alonso has deployed 3-4-3 and 4-2-3-1, neither for more than three consecutive league games. Only Tottenham have averaged more changes to their starting XI from game to game in the Premier League (and this with neither side having to rotate owing to European commitments). Chelsea have started three goalkeepers, summoning distant memories of 1996-97 when Craig Forrest, Kevin Hitchcock, Nick Colgan, Frode Grodås and Dmitri Kharine got starts between the sticks. It is little surprise the Blues have the second-worst rate in the division for conceding over their expected goal level.Much is up in the air at Stamford Bridge, yet there is a weird sense of certainty about Manchester United. They are a poor team and Carrick will surely leave soon. Alonso is a long way from the exit door but many questions need answering about his side.Explore more on these topicsChelseaManchester UnitedPremier LeagueFootball tacticsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’ | Everton | The Guardian
